728b653292cd8ac80a404a24fc7afa334d70b9e5.title: Generic cover separation
728b653292cd8ac80a404a24fc7afa334d70b9e5.body:
Let \(n\) be the ambient number of scalar latent variables, let \(G\) be a finite labeled DAG on \([n]\), let \(s\) be a sign vector, let \(\pi\) be a permutation of \([n]\), and let \(U\) be the Gaussian feature map of \cref{obj:def:cover-separated-set}, i.e. the unit-norm feature map whose kernel is \(k(a,b)=\exp\{-(a-b)^2\}\). Suppose that \(\Theta_{G,s}\) is nonempty. Then the direct-edge separation set \(\mathcal V_{G,s,\pi}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:edge-separated-set}\) is open and dense in \(\Theta_{G,s}\). Moreover,
\[
\mathcal V_{G,s,\pi}\subseteq \mathcal U_{G,s,\pi}(U),
\]
where \(\mathcal U_{G,s,\pi}(U)\) is the Gaussian-kernel ancestral-cover separation set of \(\cref{obj:def:cover-separated-set}\). The set \(\mathcal U_{G,s,\pi}(U)\) is open and dense in \(\Theta_{G,s}\), and its complement in \(\Theta_{G,s}\) is meagre, closed, and nowhere dense. If \(G\) has no directed edges, then
\[
\mathcal V_{G,s,\pi}=\Theta_{G,s}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\mathcal U_{G,s,\pi}(U)=\Theta_{G,s}.
\]

5c2686e415ec411a49aafa0b8e344d6b7f13bfb6.title: Analytic edge perturbation
5c2686e415ec411a49aafa0b8e344d6b7f13bfb6.body:
After the harmless target relabeling \(\pi=\operatorname{id}\), fix \(n\), a finite labeled DAG \(G\) on \([n]\), a sign vector \(s\), a mechanism \(\theta\in\Theta_{G,s}\) as in \cref{obj:def:model-stratum}, and an edge \(j\to i\) of \(G\). Assume that the identity-target canonical observed world generated by \(\theta\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:one-perfect-intervention-per-node}. Let \(\theta^t\) be the edge-specific affine path of \cref{obj:def:affine-path}, and write
\[
F_{ji}(\theta^t)
=
\int_{[0,1]^n}
\frac{(q_i^t(v_i))^2\bigl(q_j^t(v_j)-p_j^t(v_j\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_G(j)})\bigr)
\prod_{\ell\ne i,j}p_\ell^t(v_\ell\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_G(\ell)})}
{p_i^t(v_i\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)})}
\,dv .
\]
Then there is an open set \(O\subseteq\mathbb R\) with \([0,1]\subseteq O\) such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Integral identity.)} For every \(t\in O\), the direct-edge second-moment contrast along the path equals the displayed integral \(F_{ji}(\theta^t)\).
\item \textbf{(Analyticity.)} The map \(t\mapsto F_{ji}(\theta^t)\) is real analytic on a neighborhood of every point of \(O\).
\item \textbf{(Isolated zeros.)} If \(t\in O\) and \(F_{ji}(\theta^t)=0\), then there is \(\varepsilon>0\) such that every \(u\in(t-\varepsilon,t+\varepsilon)\) with \(u\ne t\) satisfies \(F_{ji}(\theta^u)\ne0\).
\end{itemize}
Moreover, \(F_{ji}(\theta^1)\ne0\). Finally, for every relative \(C^2\) neighborhood \(N\) of \(\theta\), there exists \(t\in(0,1)\) such that \(\theta^t\in N\), \(\theta^t\in\Theta_{G,s}\), and \(F_{ji}(\theta^t)\ne0\).

56e17dc15c987d815a69c8a061f766b3b5b73025.title: Sparse witness certificate
56e17dc15c987d815a69c8a061f766b3b5b73025.body:
For every sign vector \(s\in\{-1,1\}^3\), let \(\theta^{\mathrm{sp}}\) be the construction in \(\cref{obj:def:sparse-witness}\) and let \(\theta^{\mathrm{can}}\) be the construction in \(\cref{obj:def:cancellation-witness}\), both on the three-node DAG \(1\to2\) with node \(3\) isolated. Let \(W^{\mathrm{sp}}\) and \(W^{\mathrm{can}}\) be the corresponding observed worlds with identity mixing and identity target permutation, so that environment \(0\) has the observational law, environment \(e\) has the intervention law at target \(e\), and
\[
R_i(v)=\frac{q_i(v_i)}{p_i(v)}.
\]
Then:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sparse witness regularity.)} The mechanism \(\theta^{\mathrm{sp}}\) satisfies \(\cref{obj:ass:positive-normalized-smooth-mechanisms}\), \(\cref{obj:ass:fixed-own-derivative-sign}\) with sign vector \(s\), and \(\cref{obj:ass:faithfulness}\). Moreover, every observational conditional density \(p_i^{\mathrm{sp}}\) is \(C^\infty\) on \([0,1]^3\), and every intervention density \(q_i^{\mathrm{sp}}\) is \(C^\infty\) on \([0,1]\).
\item \textbf{(Cancellation witness regularity.)} The mechanism \(\theta^{\mathrm{can}}\) satisfies \(\cref{obj:ass:positive-normalized-smooth-mechanisms}\), \(\cref{obj:ass:fixed-own-derivative-sign}\) with sign vector \(s\), and \(\cref{obj:ass:faithfulness}\). Moreover, every observational conditional density \(p_i^{\mathrm{can}}\) is \(C^\infty\) on \([0,1]^3\), and every intervention density \(q_i^{\mathrm{can}}\) is \(C^\infty\) on \([0,1]\).
\item \textbf{(Sparse witness separation.)} The sparse witness has
\[
\frac{3}{10000}
<
\int R_2(x)^2\,dP^0_{\mathrm{sp}}(x)
-
\int R_2(x)^2\,dP^1_{\mathrm{sp}}(x),
\]
and its Gaussian-kernel population discrepancy satisfies
\[
\frac{5}{100000000}<D_{12}(W^{\mathrm{sp}}).
\]
\item \textbf{(Cancellation witness equality.)} For the cancellation witness, the law of \(R_2\) under the observational environment equals the law of \(R_2\) under environment \(1\), and
\[
D_{12}(W^{\mathrm{can}})=0.
\]
\end{itemize}

2f4c04851b9698c1619af8135b4f52b3a57ef45f.title: Exact ratio decoding
2f4c04851b9698c1619af8135b4f52b3a57ef45f.body:
Fix \(n\), a finite labelled DAG \(G\) on \([n]\), and a sign vector \(s\in\{-1,+1\}^{[n]}\).  Let \(\theta=(p_i,q_i)_{i\in[n]}\) be a mechanism on \(G\), let \(W\) be its observed world with shared mixing map \(f\), observed laws \((P^0,\ldots,P^n)\), ratios \(R_i=dP^i/dP^0\), and target permutation \(\pi\), and write \(L_i=\log R_i\).  Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Smooth positive mechanisms.)}  \(\theta\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:positive-normalized-smooth-mechanisms}.
\item \textbf{(Causal minimality.)}  \(\theta\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:causal-minimality}.
\item \textbf{(Shared mixing.)}  \(W\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:shared-diffeomorphic-mixing}.
\item \textbf{(One intervention per node.)}  \(W\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:one-perfect-intervention-per-node}.
\item \textbf{(Own-derivative signs.)}  \(\theta\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:fixed-own-derivative-sign} with sign vector \(s\).
\item \textbf{(Cover separation.)}  The stratum point \(\theta\in\Theta_{G,s}\) belongs to the cover-separated set \(\mathcal U_{G,s,\pi}\) of \cref{obj:def:cover-separated-set} for the Gaussian feature map \(\phi(a)=k(a,\cdot)\), \(k(a,b)=\exp(-(a-b)^2)\).
\end{itemize}
Let \(\mathscr D\) be the population decoder of \cref{obj:def:population-decoder}, let \(H_D=\{j\to i:D_{ji}>0\}\), and let \(G^\pi\) be the environment-label DAG.  Then
\[
\operatorname{TC}(H_D)=\operatorname{TC}(G^\pi).
\]
Moreover, the ordering selected by \(\mathscr D\) is a topological ordering of \(H_D\).  For every topological ordering of \(H_D\), with predecessor set \(B_i\) for node \(i\), the conditional-rank construction satisfies, for every \(i\in[n]\) and every \(v\) in the latent cube,
\[
U_i(f(v))=
\begin{cases}
Q_{\pi(i)}(v_{\pi(i)}), & s_{\pi(i)}=1,\\
1-Q_{\pi(i)}(v_{\pi(i)}), & s_{\pi(i)}=-1.
\end{cases}
\]
Equivalently, each displayed conditional CDF \(C_i(t\mid L_{B_i})\) agrees on the mixed latent cube with the population conditional ratio CDF
\[
C_i\bigl(t\mid L_{B_i}(f(v))\bigr)
=
\Pr_{\theta}\!\left(L_{\pi^{-1}(\pi(i))}\le t\mid L_{B_i}=L_{B_i}(f(v))\right),
\]
and the version selected by \(\mathscr D\) is the unique continuous version on the observed conditional-ratio support.

For every topological ordering of \(H_D\) and every \(i\in[n]\),
\[
\pi^{-1}\!\bigl(\operatorname{pa}_G(\pi(i))\bigr)\subseteq B_i.
\]
Under \(P^0\), for every \(A\subseteq B_i\),
\[
U_i\perp\!\!\!\perp U_{B_i\setminus A}\mid U_A
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\pi^{-1}\!\bigl(\operatorname{pa}_G(\pi(i))\bigr)\subseteq A.
\]
Consequently, for every such ordering and every \(i\), the set
\[
\pi^{-1}\!\bigl(\operatorname{pa}_G(\pi(i))\bigr)
\]
is admissible and is the unique inclusion-minimal admissible parent set.  The parent-pruned graph returned by \(\mathscr D\) is exactly \(G^\pi\), and the observed world is law-coherent.

Finally, any other DAG \(G'\), mechanism \(\theta'\), and observed world \(W'\) satisfying the same positive normalized smoothness, causal minimality, fixed own-derivative sign, shared \(C^2\)-mixing, and one-perfect-intervention-per-node conditions, and satisfying \(W'.\mathrm{law}=W.\mathrm{law}\), is componentwise \(C^2\)-equivalent to \(W\) up to the simultaneous relabeling encoded by the target permutations.  When \(n=2\), every edge \(j\to i\) of \(G\) has strictly positive observed Gaussian-MMD discrepancy,
\[
0<D_{\pi^{-1}(j),\pi^{-1}(i)}.
\]
Within this regime, \(\mathscr D\) improves the arbitrary-dimensional intervention count of \citet[Theorem~3.4]{vonKugelgenEtAl2023UnknownInterventions} from two perfect interventions per node to one, extends the decoding and uniqueness conclusions from faithful mechanisms to causal-minimal mechanisms, supplies the continuous law-separation witness used by \citet[Theorem~3.2]{vonKugelgenEtAl2023UnknownInterventions} when \(n=2\), and recovers the graph, topological order, and intervention alignment that are inputs in \citet[Theorem~4.2]{WendongEtAl2023CauCA} and \citet[Corollary~{D}.1]{YaoEtAl2025InvariancePrinciple}.

d4467bf359714a9a935c3891d835255d74987947.title: Simultaneous confidence edges
d4467bf359714a9a935c3891d835255d74987947.body:
Fix \(n\ge 1\), a labeled DAG \(G\) on \([n]\), a sign vector \(s\), a mechanism \(\theta\), an observed world with target permutation \(\pi\), and a sample-split experiment \(S\). Suppose:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Structural model.)} The mechanism, shared mixing representation, and one-intervention-per-node design satisfy \(\cref{obj:ass:positive-normalized-smooth-mechanisms,obj:ass:shared-diffeomorphic-mixing,obj:ass:one-perfect-intervention-per-node}\).
\item \textbf{(Sample splitting.)} The training and evaluation folds satisfy \(\cref{obj:ass:independent-environment-sampling}\), and each environment has evaluation sample size \(N_e\ge 1\).
\item \textbf{(Levels.)} The familywise evaluation level and first-stage failure level satisfy \(\alpha,\eta\in(0,1)\).
\item \textbf{(First-stage event.)} With
\[
\mathcal E_{\mathrm{fs}}
=
\left\{
\omega:
\forall i\in[n],\ \forall e\in\{0,\ldots,n\},\
\int
\left|\widehat R_i(x)-R_i(x)\right|
\,dP^e(x)
\le a_N(\eta)
\right\},
\]
where the displayed integrals are finite, the training-fold event obeys
\[
\Pr(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{fs}})\ge 1-\eta .
\]
\end{itemize}
Let \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{MMD}}\) be the simultaneous evaluation event
\[
\mathcal E_{\mathrm{MMD}}
=
\left\{
\omega:
\forall j\ne i,\
\left|\widehat D_{ji}(\omega)-D_{ji}\right|
\le \varepsilon_N(\alpha,\eta)
\right\}.
\]
Then, conditionally on the training fold and on \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{fs}}\), this event has probability at least \(1-\alpha\): for every training-fold measurable event \(B\),
\[
(1-\alpha)\Pr(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{fs}}\cap B)
\le
\Pr(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{MMD}}\cap\mathcal E_{\mathrm{fs}}\cap B).
\]
Consequently,
\[
\Pr(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{MMD}})\ge 1-\alpha-\eta .
\]
Moreover, for every \(\omega\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{MMD}}\), every selected arrow \(j\to i\) of the sample-split confidence graph \(\widehat H\) from \(\cref{obj:def:sample-split-confidence-graph}\) satisfies that \(\pi(j)\) is an ancestor of \(\pi(i)\) in \(G\). If, in addition,
\[
2\varepsilon_N(\alpha,\eta)<D_{ji}
\qquad
\text{for every }j,i\text{ such that }\pi(j)\lessdot_G \pi(i),
\]
then for every \(\omega\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{MMD}}\),
\[
\operatorname{TC}\!\left(\widehat H(\omega)\right)
=
\operatorname{TC}\!\left(G^\pi\right).
\]

7ef42b644655ecdccfd1f1ba43705c84c9ddc262.title: Conditional RKHS mean bound
7ef42b644655ecdccfd1f1ba43705c84c9ddc262.body:
Fix \(n\ge 1\), a labeled DAG \(G\) on \([n]\), a mechanism \(\theta\), an observed world with environment laws \(P^0,\ldots,P^n\), and a sample-split experiment \(S\). Let \(\mathcal H_k\) be a complete real Hilbert space equipped with a measurable unit-norm feature map \(\phi\) for the Gaussian kernel \(k(a,b)=\exp(-(a-b)^2)\).

Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Conditional evaluation sampling.)} The experiment satisfies the conditional evaluation-sampling conditions: the ambient and environment laws are probability measures; the complete training fold is measurable; the evaluation observations are measurable, independent within each environment, distributed according to their corresponding \(P^e\), and independent of the training fold; and the fitted ratio map is jointly measurable in the training fold and the evaluation point.
\item \textbf{(Evaluation sizes.)} Each environment has at least one evaluation observation, \(N_e\ge 1\) for every \(e\in\{0,\ldots,n\}\). Write
\[
\underline N=\min_{0\le e\le n}N_e .
\]
\item \textbf{(Familywise level.)} The error level satisfies \(\alpha\in(0,1)\).
\end{itemize}

For each training realization, let \(\widehat R_i\) denote the fitted ratio obtained from the complete training fold, and define
\[
\widehat \mu_{e i}
=
\frac{1}{N_e}\sum_{r=1}^{N_e}\phi\!\left(\widehat R_i(X_{er})\right),
\qquad
\mu_{e i}
=
\mathbb E_{X\sim P^e}\!\left[\phi\!\left(\widehat R_i(X)\right)\right].
\]
Then, conditionally on the complete training fold, the simultaneous event
\[
\forall i\in[n]\ \forall e\in\{0,\ldots,n\},\qquad
\left\|\widehat \mu_{e i}-\mu_{e i}\right\|_{\mathcal H_k}
\le
\frac{1+\sqrt{2\log\!\left(n(n+1)/\alpha\right)}}{\sqrt{\underline N}}
\]
has probability at least \(1-\alpha\). Equivalently, for every event \(B\) measurable with respect to the complete training fold,
\[
(1-\alpha)\mathbb P(B)
\le
\mathbb P\!\left(
B\cap
\left\{
\forall i\in[n]\ \forall e\in\{0,\ldots,n\},\
\left\|\widehat \mu_{e i}-\mu_{e i}\right\|_{\mathcal H_k}
\le
\frac{1+\sqrt{2\log\!\left(n(n+1)/\alpha\right)}}{\sqrt{\underline N}}
\right\}
\right).
\]

25fd8d5a8960586efe10843bdd4bad4ef5a0a74c.title: Positive smooth mechanisms
25fd8d5a8960586efe10843bdd4bad4ef5a0a74c.body: For every \(i\in[n]\), the observational mechanism \(p_i\) and the intervention density \(q_i\) are strictly positive, normalized \(C^3\) densities on their respective closed cubes.

a895888c4e6f19d84d3c91e622a880b09568e6d7.title: Faithful observational law
a895888c4e6f19d84d3c91e622a880b09568e6d7.body: The observational latent density \(p^0\) is faithful to the DAG \(G\).

6d057fbd2d92b1d938c21a11eee347231d6889e8.title: Shared diffeomorphic mixing
6d057fbd2d92b1d938c21a11eee347231d6889e8.body: The same map \(f\) is a \(C^2\) diffeomorphism from \([0,1]^n\) onto \(\mathcal X\) in every environment.

7b873191cae07ab3ad268e5b8494799ca4ada26b.title: One intervention per node
7b873191cae07ab3ad268e5b8494799ca4ada26b.body: Together with the known observational law \(P^0\), the laws \(P^1,\ldots,P^n\) arise from distinct unknown targets. Each interventional law replaces exactly one mechanism \(p_i\) by the corresponding parent-independent density \(q_i\).

d3fe12461eae7f63244c6c2e3d683b4ab8927654.title: Fixed derivative sign
d3fe12461eae7f63244c6c2e3d683b4ab8927654.body:
For every \(i\in[n]\),
\[
s_i\,\partial_{v_i}\log\{q_i(v_i)/p_i(v_i\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)})\}>0
\]
throughout the closed cube.

38acc46cfa1aa5d2090d8d5fc94971c620c551bd.title: Independent environment sampling
38acc46cfa1aa5d2090d8d5fc94971c620c551bd.body: Within each environment \(e\), the \(N_e\) observations are independent draws from \(P^e\), and the training and evaluation folds are independent.

756264c254abdf3e260648904fe3bc57c3f4ee40.title: Hölder radius bound
756264c254abdf3e260648904fe3bc57c3f4ee40.body: For every \(i\in[n]\), the conditional density \(p_i\), the intervention density \(q_i\), and the latent-coordinate log-ratio \(L_i\circ f\) have Hölder norm of order \(\beta\) at most \(M\).

cece7ae00ba9522491dbfdc61784866717758b72.title: Density lower envelope
cece7ae00ba9522491dbfdc61784866717758b72.body: For every \(i\in[n]\), the densities \(p_i\) and \(q_i\) are bounded below by \(c\) on their respective closed cubes.

188a013ab4cf79f6f14ff510256c57bef74b2c96.title: Own-derivative margin
188a013ab4cf79f6f14ff510256c57bef74b2c96.body:
For every \(i\in[n]\) and every \(v\in[0,1]^n\),
\[
s_i\,\partial_{v_i}L_i(f(v))\ge c.
\]

06104421d0a9feeb48ca3a27043ed8a90bb4e349.title: Shared mixing geometry
06104421d0a9feeb48ca3a27043ed8a90bb4e349.body:
The shared mixing map satisfies
\[
\max\left\{
\|f\|_{C^2([0,1]^n)},
\|f^{-1}\|_{C^2(\mathcal X)},
\sup_{v\in[0,1]^n}|\det Df(v)|,
\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}|\det Df^{-1}(x)|
\right\}\le M.
\]

19fdcede127707760221bea3336b8a859471645c.title: Conditional design envelope
19fdcede127707760221bea3336b8a859471645c.body:
For every \(i\in[n]\), the density \(g_i\) of \(L_{B_i}(X)\) under \(P^i\) satisfies
\[
c\le g_i(z)\le M
\]
for all \(z\in\mathcal Z_i(K)\).

e59a12eda5db605a2b76b46fba5dc8fefa9f08c4.title: Causal minimality
e59a12eda5db605a2b76b46fba5dc8fefa9f08c4.body:
For every edge \(j\to i\) of \(G\), the observational law \(p^0\) satisfies
\[
V_i\not\!\perp\!\!\!\perp V_j
\mid
V_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)\setminus\{j\}} .
\]

1351b19493ea4b09e459aa69b3c8ee91c6c319ab.title: Model stratum \(\Theta_{G,s}\)

4f6f118b8c4bd42c02b9c0d07b1eb9968be56a59.title: Edge-separated set \(\mathcal V_{G,s,\pi}\)
4f6f118b8c4bd42c02b9c0d07b1eb9968be56a59.body:
\[
\mathcal V_{G,s,\pi}
=
\left\{
\theta\in\Theta_{G,s}:
F_{\pi^{-1}(j),\pi^{-1}(i)}(\theta)\ne0
\text{ for every edge }j\to i\text{ of }G
\right\}.
\]

89302b4dca11946dcbf4385bebc3cc500a4c10ef.title: Sparse witness \(\theta^{\mathrm{sp}}\)
89302b4dca11946dcbf4385bebc3cc500a4c10ef.body:
On the graph \(1\to2\) with node \(3\) isolated, define \(\theta^{\mathrm{sp}}\) by
\[
h(z)=2z-1,
\]
\[
q_i(z)=\frac{4\exp(4z)}{\exp(4)-1},
\]
\[
p_2(y\mid x)=1+0.1h(x)h(y),
\]
and
\[
p_1=p_3=1.
\]
For a sign vector with a negative prescribed sign in coordinate \(i\), the corresponding coordinate is reflected by the map \(z\mapsto1-z\).

8f8a6d09c8500cd50ae56d10c144a6654624278c.title: Generated-rank handle \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{rank}}\)
8f8a6d09c8500cd50ae56d10c144a6654624278c.body: \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{rank}}\) is the proposed local-linear conditional-CDF and generated-covariate analysis handle for rank coordinates formed from cross-fitted log-ratio responses and conditioning covariates. It adapts the local-linear conditional-CDF estimator of Xie to this generated-regressor setting by decomposing the second-stage rank error into the oracle conditional-CDF process, indicator boundary crossings from the generated threshold, and local-design perturbations from generated conditioning arguments. The last component is then linearized using the generated-covariate expansion of Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle.

3fcd3ee67b491f3afb560fcd341c1e2357e3337b.title: Generated-rank frontier
3fcd3ee67b491f3afb560fcd341c1e2357e3337b.body:
A natural next question is whether the handle \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{rank}}\) yields uniform generated-rank estimators under the following conditions:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(First-stage contract.)}
\[
\inf_{\theta\in\Theta^{\beta}_{G,s}(c,M,K,\rho)}
\Pr_\theta\{\mathcal E_N^{\infty}(b_N)\}\ge 1-\eta_N .
\]
\item \textbf{(Bandwidth scale.)} The bandwidth \(h_N\) satisfies \(h_N\to0\),
\[
b_N=o(h_N),
\]
and
\[
\frac{\underline N h_N^{d_\star}}{\log(\underline N)}\to\infty .
\]
\end{itemize}
The target is a construction of cross-fitted estimators \(\widehat U_i\) such that
\[
\max_{i\in[n]}\|\widehat U_i-U_i\|_{\infty,K}
=
O_{\Pr,\Theta^{\beta}_{G,s}(c,M,K,\rho)}(r_N),
\]
where
\[
r_N
=
h_N^2+
\sqrt{\frac{\log(\underline N)}{\underline N h_N^{d_\star}}}
+\frac{b_N}{h_N}.
\]
When the first-stage log-ratio estimators additionally admit a uniform asymptotically linear representation on \(K\), future work could derive the corresponding expansion for \(\widehat U_i-U_i\), separating threshold crossings, generated-conditioning perturbations, oracle conditional-CDF variance, and smoothing bias, and could characterize the weakest sufficient first-stage remainder bound.

ac8130afd26d5a7eac01c17c289d2e1d1c119a74.title: Affine path $\theta^t$
ac8130afd26d5a7eac01c17c289d2e1d1c119a74.body:
For \(\theta=((p_i,q_i))_{i=1}^{n}\in\Theta_{G,s}\), an edge \(j\to i\), and \(t\in[0,1]\), let the reflected edge-specific embedding of \(\theta^{\mathrm{sp}}\) in \(G\) have coordinates \(((p_\ell^{\mathrm{sp}},q_\ell^{\mathrm{sp}}))_{\ell=1}^n\). The affine path \(\theta^t\) is the mechanism with coordinates
\[
p_\ell^t=(1-t)p_\ell+t p_\ell^{\mathrm{sp}},
\qquad
q_\ell^t=(1-t)q_\ell+t q_\ell^{\mathrm{sp}},
\qquad \ell\in[n].
\]

f1741816405a4d21c8ce0661e13e4ffd1a8e08ea.title: Cancellation witness $\theta^{\mathrm{can}}$
f1741816405a4d21c8ce0661e13e4ffd1a8e08ea.body:
On the graph \(1\to2\) with node \(3\) isolated, define \(\theta^{\mathrm{can}}\) by
\[
q_i(z)=\frac{4\exp(4z)}{\exp(4)-1},
\qquad
p_1=1,
\qquad
p_3=1,
\]
\[
h(y)=2y-1,
\qquad
H(x)=\frac{\exp(4x)-1}{\exp(4)-1}-x,
\qquad
p_2(y\mid x)=1+0.1H(x)h(y).
\]
For any other sign vector, \(\theta^{\mathrm{can}}\) is obtained from this mechanism by coordinate reflections.

b4e08a19a8623b307fe220553eef7f05b40b0717.title: Population decoder $\mathscr D$
b4e08a19a8623b307fe220553eef7f05b40b0717.body:
Given observed laws \((P^0,\ldots,P^n)\), the population decoder \(\mathscr D\) is defined by the following steps.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Compute the likelihood ratios and log-ratios
\[
R_i=\frac{dP^i}{dP^0},
\qquad
L_i=\log R_i,
\qquad i\in[n],
\]
and the Gaussian-MMD discrepancies \(D_{ji}\).

\item Form the observable directed ratio-discrepancy graph
\[
H_D=\{j\to i:j\ne i\text{ and }D_{ji}>0\}.
\]

\item Choose a topological ordering of \(H_D\). For each \(i\), let \(B_i\) be the predecessors of \(i\) in that ordering and define
\[
U_i=C_i(L_i\mid L_{B_i}).
\]

\item Align environment \(i\) with coordinate \(U_i\).

\item For each \(i\), range over \(A\subseteq B_i\) and identify the unique inclusion-minimal subset satisfying
\[
U_i\mathbin{\perp\!\!\!\perp}_{P^0}U_{B_i\setminus A}\mid U_A.
\]
The output is the environment-label DAG
\[
G^\pi_{\mathscr D}
=
\{a\to i:\ a\in A_i^{\min}\},
\qquad
A_i^{\min}
=
\min_{\subseteq}
\left\{
A\subseteq B_i:
U_i\mathbin{\perp\!\!\!\perp}_{P^0}U_{B_i\setminus A}\mid U_A
\right\}.
\]
\end{enumerate}

661c6c902aec71797cfd8f9cf5bcbc3eaa6526d1.title: Sample-split confidence graph $\widehat H$
661c6c902aec71797cfd8f9cf5bcbc3eaa6526d1.body:
Under \(\cref{obj:ass:independent-environment-sampling}\), with training and evaluation folds and tuning levels \(\alpha,\eta\), the sample-split confidence graph \(\widehat H\) is defined by the following steps.
\begin{enumerate}
\item On the training folds, fit likelihood-ratio estimators
\[
\widehat R_i,
\qquad i\in[n].
\]

\item On the independent evaluation folds, compute the empirical Gaussian-MMD discrepancies
\[
\widehat D_{ji},
\qquad j,i\in[n],\ j\ne i,
\]
using \(\widehat R_i\).

\item Output the directed graph
\[
\widehat H
=
\left\{
j\to i:
\widehat D_{ji}-\varepsilon_N(\alpha,\eta)>0
\right\}.
\]
\end{enumerate}

9fd89d6282bb434879cebfbef832b5f0f921a6e0.title: Bounded Hölder subclass $\Theta^{\beta}_{G,s}(c,M,K,\rho)$
9fd89d6282bb434879cebfbef832b5f0f921a6e0.body:
The bounded Hölder subclass is
\[
\Theta^{\beta}_{G,s}(c,M,K,\rho)
=
\left\{
\theta\in\Theta_{G,s}:
\begin{array}{l}
\text{\(\cref{obj:ass:bounded-holder-radius}\) holds for } n,G,s,\beta,c,M,K,\rho,\\
\text{\(\cref{obj:ass:density-lower-envelope}\) holds for } n,G,s,\beta,c,M,K,\rho,\\
\text{\(\cref{obj:ass:own-derivative-margin}\) holds for } n,G,s,\beta,c,M,K,\rho,\\
\text{\(\cref{obj:ass:common-interior-domain}\) holds for } n,G,s,\beta,c,M,K,\rho,\\
\text{\(\cref{obj:ass:bounded-shared-mixing-geometry}\) holds for } n,G,s,\beta,c,M,K,\rho,\\
\text{\(\cref{obj:ass:observed-log-ratio-regularity}\) holds for } n,G,s,\beta,c,M,K,\rho,\\
\text{\(\cref{obj:ass:conditional-design-envelope}\) holds for } n,G,s,\beta,c,M,K,\rho
\end{array}
\right\}.
\]

9dc0cebce647f3c999334a764565843028558468.title: First-stage event $\mathcal E_N^{\infty}(b_N)$
9dc0cebce647f3c999334a764565843028558468.body:
The simultaneous \(C^1\) first-stage log-ratio accuracy event is
\[
\mathcal E_N^{\infty}(b_N)
=
\left\{
\max_{i\in[n]}
\left\|
\log\widehat R_i-\log R_i
\right\|_{C^1(\mathcal X)}
\le b_N
\right\}.
\]
The first-stage contract is
\[
\inf_{\theta\in\Theta^{\beta}_{G,s}(c,M,K,\rho)}
\Pr_\theta\left\{\mathcal E_N^{\infty}(b_N)\right\}
\ge 1-\eta_N.
\]

7397a5929cdace98375cfb69b632b147fb346987.title: Latent state space
7397a5929cdace98375cfb69b632b147fb346987.body:
For \(n\in\mathbb N\), the latent state \(V=(V_1,\ldots,V_n)\) ranges over the real coordinate space
\[
\mathbb R^{[n]}=\{v:[n]\to\mathbb R\}.
\]

f89886bf755c217c450b71349d638d273e9d4ba5.title: Observational product density
f89886bf755c217c450b71349d638d273e9d4ba5.body:
For a finite dimension \(n\), a labeled DAG \(G\) on \([n]\), a mechanism \(\theta\) with observational conditional-density carriers \(p_i\), and a latent state \(v=(v_1,\ldots,v_n)\in\mathbb R^n\), define
\[
p^0(v)=\prod_{i=1}^n p_i\bigl(v_i\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)}\bigr).
\]

f601e5ef073078fa40949c7ee437804535707d85.title: Intervention distribution function
f601e5ef073078fa40949c7ee437804535707d85.body:
For a mechanism \(\theta\) on a DAG \(G\) over \([n]\), with parent-independent intervention density \(q_i\) at coordinate \(i\), define
\[
Q_i(v)=\int_0^v q_i(u)\,du
\]
for \(i\in[n]\) and \(v\in\mathbb R\).

a419d8623ecbe068cfff4ff791e3f845f81a3d6d.title: Ancestral cover relation
a419d8623ecbe068cfff4ff791e3f845f81a3d6d.body:
For a DAG \(G\) on the finite labeled vertex set \([n]\), define \(j\lessdot_G i\) to be the cover relation in the ancestor order of \(G\):
\[
j\lessdot_G i
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
j <_G i
\;\;\text{and}\;\;
\{k\in[n]: j <_G k <_G i\}=\varnothing .
\]

982d1989e1b019c4230f02382bde4bf6b4463ae8.title: Sample-split experiment
982d1989e1b019c4230f02382bde4bf6b4463ae8.body:
A sample-split experiment for a fixed observed environment family \(W\), with latent state space \(\mathbb R^n\), consists of a measurable sample space \(\Omega\) together with:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Experiment law.)} A probability measure on \(\Omega\).
\item \textbf{(Evaluation fold.)} Environment sample sizes \(N_e\in\mathbb N\), for \(e=0,\ldots,n\), and evaluation observations
\[
X^{\mathrm{eval}}_{e,m}:\Omega\to\mathbb R^n,
\qquad
m=1,\ldots,N_e .
\]
\item \textbf{(Training fold.)} Training sample sizes \(N^{\mathrm{tr}}_e\in\mathbb N\), for \(e=0,\ldots,n\), and training observations
\[
X^{\mathrm{tr}}_{e,m}:\Omega\to\mathbb R^n,
\qquad
m=1,\ldots,N^{\mathrm{tr}}_e .
\]
\item \textbf{(Fitted ratios.)} For each full training fold \(T=\{T_{e,m}:e=0,\ldots,n,\ m=1,\ldots,N^{\mathrm{tr}}_e\}\), each \(i\in[n]\), and each \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), a fitted ratio value
\[
\widehat R_i(T,x)\in\mathbb R .
\]
The map \((T,x)\mapsto \widehat R_i(T,x)\) is jointly measurable for every \(i\), the map \(x\mapsto \widehat R_i(T,x)\) is measurable for every \(T\) and \(i\), and
\[
\widehat R_i(T,x)>0
\]
for every \(T\), \(i\), and \(x\).
\item \textbf{(First-stage radius.)} A first-stage radius \(a_N(\eta)\in\mathbb R\), indexed by the first-stage failure level \(\eta\), satisfying
\[
a_N(\eta)\ge 0
\]
for every \(\eta\in\mathbb R\).
\item \textbf{(Error levels.)} A familywise evaluation error level \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) and a first-stage failure level \(\eta\in(0,1)\).
\end{itemize}

a8e36834e62f75dcd1ec37f98da5728a47703701.title: Bounded regime parameters
a8e36834e62f75dcd1ec37f98da5728a47703701.body:
For an observed world \(W\), a bounded generated-rank regime consists of:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Order.)} An order map \(o:[n]\to\mathbb N\).
\item \textbf{(Environment sample sizes.)} A sample-size sequence \(N_e(N)\in\mathbb N\) for each \(N\in\mathbb N\) and each environment \(e\in\{0,\ldots,n\}\).
\item \textbf{(First-stage ratio rate.)} A uniform first-stage \(C^1\) rate \(b_N\) satisfying
\[
b_N>0\quad\text{for every }N,
\qquad
b_N\to 0.
\]
\item \textbf{(First-stage failure rate.)} A first-stage failure sequence \(\eta_N\) satisfying
\[
\eta_N>0\quad\text{for every }N,
\qquad
\eta_N\to 0.
\]
\item \textbf{(Second-stage bandwidth.)} A second-stage bandwidth \(h_N\) satisfying
\[
h_N>0\quad\text{for every }N,
\qquad
h_N\to 0.
\]
\end{itemize}

a175e7176a9fba4a73471eca56c0d22c08675760.title: Maximum conditioning dimension
a175e7176a9fba4a73471eca56c0d22c08675760.body:
The maximum conditioning dimension of the selected ordering is
\[
d_\star := \max_{i\in[n]} |B_i|,
\]
where \(B_i\) is the set of labels preceding \(i\) in that ordering.

9934b30b9768ef1240a873f05a037215290debd5.title: Componentwise \(C^2\) equivalence
9934b30b9768ef1240a873f05a037215290debd5.body:
For two observed worlds \(W_1\) over \((G_1,\theta_1)\) and \(W_2\) over \((G_2,\theta_2)\), with the same ambient number \(n\) of scalar latent variables, write
\[
\mathcal X_m=\{W_m.\mathrm{mix}(v):v\in[0,1]^n\},\qquad m=1,2.
\]
The worlds \(W_1\) and \(W_2\) are componentwise \(C^2\)-equivalent when the following conditions hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Observed support.)} Their observed supports agree, \(\mathcal X_1=\mathcal X_2\).
\item \textbf{(DAG relabeling.)} There is a permutation \(\sigma\) of \([n]\) such that, for every \(j,i\in[n]\),
\[
\sigma(j)\to_{G_2}\sigma(i)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
j\to_{G_1} i.
\]
\item \textbf{(Target alignment.)} For every environment label \(e\), the target coordinate of \(W_2\) in environment \(e\) is \(\sigma\) applied to the target coordinate of \(W_1\) in environment \(e\).
\item \textbf{(Coordinate changes.)} There are functions \(h_i:[0,1]\to[0,1]\) and \(h_i^{-1}:[0,1]\to[0,1]\), one pair for each \(i\in[n]\), each \(C^2\) on \([0,1]\), such that for every \(i\in[n]\) and every \(z\in[0,1]\),
\[
h_i^{-1}(h_i(z))=z,
\qquad
h_i(h_i^{-1}(z))=z.
\]
\item \textbf{(Unmixing relation.)} For every \(x\in\mathcal X_1\) and every \(i\in[n]\),
\[
W_2.\mathrm{unmix}(x)_{\sigma(i)}
=
h_i\!\left(W_1.\mathrm{unmix}(x)_i\right).
\]
\end{itemize}

1ecce3985edd345cffcfa0a0f50f804d5dbce38a.title: Density lower envelope
1ecce3985edd345cffcfa0a0f50f804d5dbce38a.body:
For the bounded regime under consideration, the lower-envelope constant \(c\) satisfies:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Range.)} \(0<c<1\).
\item \textbf{(Observational densities.)} For every \(i\in[n]\) and every latent state \(v\in[0,1]^n\),
\[
c\le p_i(v_i\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)}).
\]
\item \textbf{(Intervention densities.)} For every \(i\in[n]\) and every \(z\in[0,1]\),
\[
c\le q_i(z).
\]
\end{itemize}

35bf154e435bbf4476e4b8a2df490612511787fe.title: Bounded Hölder radius
35bf154e435bbf4476e4b8a2df490612511787fe.body:
Let \(k=\lfloor \beta\rfloor\). The parameters satisfy \(2<\beta\) and \(1<M\). For every \(i\in[n]\), the three functions
\[
p_i,\qquad q_i,\qquad v\mapsto L_i(f(v))
\]
satisfy the common Hölder bound of order \(\beta\) and radius \(M\) on their respective domains: \(p_i\) and \(v\mapsto L_i(f(v))\) on \([0,1]^n\), and \(q_i\) on \([0,1]\). That is, for each such function \(r\) with domain \(K\), \(r\) is \(C^k\) on \(K\),
\[
\|D^m r(z)\|\le M
\]
for every \(m\le k\) and every \(z\in K\), and
\[
\|D^k r(z)-D^k r(z')\|\le M\|z-z'\|^{\beta-k}
\]
for every \(z,z'\in K\).

1b53d0605d110589064a35954b8352555515dc8b.title: Independent environment sampling
1b53d0605d110589064a35954b8352555515dc8b.body:
The sample-split experiment is defined on a probability space, and for each environment \(e\), the observed law \(P^e\) is a probability measure. It satisfies:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Training fold.)} Within each environment \(e\), the training observations are independent, and every training observation in environment \(e\) has law \(P^e\).
\item \textbf{(Evaluation fold.)} Within each environment \(e\), the evaluation observations are independent, and every evaluation observation in environment \(e\) has law \(P^e\).
\item \textbf{(Fold independence.)} The complete training fold is independent of the complete evaluation fold.
\item \textbf{(First-stage measurability.)} The ratio estimate \(\widehat R_i(x)\) is measurable with respect to the training fold, both pointwise in \(x\) and jointly in the training fold and latent state \(x\). The event
\[
\left\{\omega:\ \forall i\in[n],\ \forall e,\ 
\int \left|\widehat R_i(x)-R_i(x)\right|\,dP^e(x)\le a_N
\ \text{with finite integral}\right\}
\]
is measurable with respect to the training fold.
\end{itemize}

b8e93f7754ae5bbed6bc574845094a293d00fc80.title: Perfect intervention laws
b8e93f7754ae5bbed6bc574845094a293d00fc80.body:
For the mechanism \(\theta\), the shared mixing map \(f\), the observed laws \(P^0,\ldots,P^n\), the target permutation \(\pi\), and the supplied likelihood ratios \(R_1,\ldots,R_n\), the following conditions hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Observational pushforward.)} The observational law satisfies
\[
P^0
=
f_\#\bigl(p^0(v)\,dv\bigr),
\qquad
p^0(v)=\prod_{i=1}^n p_i(v_i\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)}),
\]
with \(v\in[0,1]^n\).
\item \textbf{(Single-target pushforwards.)} For every environment \(e\in[n]\),
\[
P^e
=
f_\#\bigl(p^{\pi(e)}(v)\,dv\bigr),
\qquad
p^{\pi(e)}(v)
=
q_{\pi(e)}(v_{\pi(e)})
\prod_{\ell\ne \pi(e)}
p_\ell(v_\ell\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_G(\ell)}).
\]
\item \textbf{(Radon--Nikodym ratios.)} For every \(e\in[n]\),
\[
R_e(X)=\frac{dP^e}{dP^0}(X)
\quad\text{\(P^0\)-almost surely.}
\]
\item \textbf{(Latent ratio formula.)} For every \(e\in[n]\) and every \(v\in[0,1]^n\),
\[
R_e(f(v))
=
\frac{q_{\pi(e)}(v_{\pi(e)})}
{p_{\pi(e)}(v_{\pi(e)}\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_G(\pi(e))})}.
\]
\end{itemize}

9f42d989e294850d68c4b576c2fc77788754c067.title: Common interior domain
9f42d989e294850d68c4b576c2fc77788754c067.body:
The common interior-domain condition for \(K\) and radius \(\rho\) is the conjunction:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Radius.)} \(0<\rho<1/2\).
\item \textbf{(Compactness.)} \(K\) is compact.
\item \textbf{(Observed interior.)} \(K\subseteq \operatorname{int}(\mathcal X)\), where \(\mathcal X=f([0,1]^n)\).
\item \textbf{(Latent boundary margin.)} For every \(v\in f^{-1}(K)\),
\[
\rho\le \operatorname{dist}\bigl(v,\partial[0,1]^n\bigr).
\]
\end{itemize}

e358728c56d9efd475484a1148e46526f883d66b.title: First-stage ratio contract
e358728c56d9efd475484a1148e46526f883d66b.body:
For a generated observed-world assignment \(W_\theta\), a decoder-selected bounded-regime assignment \(R_\theta\), sample-split experiments \(S_{\theta,N}\), a common environment sample-size sequence \(N\mapsto (N_e(N))_{e=0}^n\), rate sequences \(b_N\) and \(\eta_N\), and subclass parameters \(\beta,c,M,K,\rho\), define
\[
\mathcal E_N^{\infty}(b_N)
=
\left\{
\omega:
\begin{array}{l}
\text{for every } i\in[n],\ 
\log \widehat R_i(\omega,\cdot)\text{ and }L_i\text{ are }C^1\text{ on }\mathcal X,\\
\text{and for every }x\in\mathcal X,\ 
\left|\log \widehat R_i(\omega,x)-L_i(x)\right|\le b_N,\\
\left\|D_x\log \widehat R_i(\omega,x)-D_xL_i(x)\right\|\le b_N
\end{array}
\right\}.
\]
The first-stage ratio contract holds when the following conditions are satisfied:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Vanishing positive rates.)} For every \(N\), \(b_N>0\) and \(\eta_N>0\), and both sequences satisfy \(b_N\to0\) and \(\eta_N\to0\) as \(N\to\infty\).
\item \textbf{(Common selected-regime schedules.)} For every \(N\) and every \(\theta\in\Theta^{\beta}_{G,s}(c,M,K,\rho)\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:bounded-holder-subclass}\), the selected bounded regime \(R_\theta\) has environment sample-size sequence \(N\mapsto (N_e(N))_{e=0}^n\), ratio-error rate \(b_N\), and first-stage failure rate \(\eta_N\).
\item \textbf{(Sampling design.)} For every \(N\) and every \(\theta\in\Theta^{\beta}_{G,s}(c,M,K,\rho)\), the experiment \(S_{\theta,N}\) satisfies the independent-environment sample-splitting conditions in \(\cref{obj:ass:independent-environment-sampling}\), and its environment sample sizes are exactly \((N_e(N))_{e=0}^n\).
\item \textbf{(Measurable high-probability event.)} For every \(N\) and every \(\theta\in\Theta^{\beta}_{G,s}(c,M,K,\rho)\), the event \(\mathcal E_N^{\infty}(b_N)\) is measurable under \(S_{\theta,N}\), and
\[
1-\eta_N
\le
\Pr_{S_{\theta,N}}\left\{\mathcal E_N^{\infty}(b_N)\right\}.
\]
\end{itemize}

3ef6e33e25f57ac1290907522a8083daf5122585.title: Exact ratio decoding
3ef6e33e25f57ac1290907522a8083daf5122585.body:
Fix \(n\), a finite labelled DAG \(G\) on \([n]\), and a sign vector \(s\in\{-1,+1\}^{[n]}\).  Let \(\theta=(p_i,q_i)_{i\in[n]}\) be a mechanism on \(G\), let \(W\) be its observed world with shared mixing map \(f\), observed laws \((P^0,\ldots,P^n)\), likelihood ratios \(R_i=dP^i/dP^0\), and target permutation \(\pi\), and write \(L_i=\log R_i\).  Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Smooth positive mechanisms.)}  \(\theta\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:positive-normalized-smooth-mechanisms}.
\item \textbf{(Causal minimality.)}  \(\theta\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:causal-minimality}.
\item \textbf{(Shared mixing.)}  \(W\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:shared-diffeomorphic-mixing}.
\item \textbf{(One intervention per node.)}  \(W\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:one-perfect-intervention-per-node}.
\item \textbf{(Own-derivative signs.)}  \(\theta\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:fixed-own-derivative-sign} with sign vector \(s\).
\item \textbf{(Cover separation.)}  The stratum point \(\theta\in\Theta_{G,s}\) belongs to the cover-separated set \(\mathcal U_{G,s,\pi}\) of \cref{obj:def:cover-separated-set} for the Gaussian feature map \(\phi(a)=k(a,\cdot)\), \(k(a,b)=\exp(-(a-b)^2)\).
\end{itemize}
Let \(\mathscr D\) be the population decoder of \cref{obj:def:population-decoder}, let \(H_D=\{j\to i:D_{ji}>0\}\), and let \(G^\pi\) be the environment-label DAG.  Then
\[
\operatorname{TC}(H_D)=\operatorname{TC}(G^\pi).
\]
Moreover, the ordering selected by \(\mathscr D\) is a topological ordering of \(H_D\).  For every topological ordering of \(H_D\), with predecessor set \(B_i\) for node \(i\), and every \(i\in[n]\), the selected conditional CDF \(C_i(t\mid L_{B_i})\) is a continuous version of the conditional ratio CDF.  At the mixed latent point \(f(v)\), every continuous version has a representative agreeing with the population conditional ratio CDF determined by \(\theta\), target \(\pi(i)\), threshold \(t\), and latent state \(v\); the version selected by \(\mathscr D\) is the unique continuous version on the observed conditional-ratio support.  Consequently, for every \(v\) in the latent cube,
\[
U_i(f(v))=
\begin{cases}
Q_{\pi(i)}(v_{\pi(i)}), & s_{\pi(i)}=1,\\
1-Q_{\pi(i)}(v_{\pi(i)}), & s_{\pi(i)}=-1.
\end{cases}
\]
For every topological ordering of \(H_D\) and every \(i\in[n]\),
\[
\pi^{-1}\!\bigl(\operatorname{pa}_G(\pi(i))\bigr)\subseteq B_i.
\]
Under \(P^0\), for every such ordering, every \(i\in[n]\), and every \(A\subseteq B_i\),
\[
U_i\perp\!\!\!\perp U_{B_i\setminus A}\mid U_A
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\pi^{-1}\!\bigl(\operatorname{pa}_G(\pi(i))\bigr)\subseteq A.
\]
Thus, for every such ordering and every \(i\), the set
\[
\pi^{-1}\!\bigl(\operatorname{pa}_G(\pi(i))\bigr)
\]
is admissible and is the unique inclusion-minimal admissible parent set.  The observed laws are coherent with the displayed observed world: the same family \((P^0,\ldots,P^n)\) supplies the decoder inputs, the likelihood ratios \(R_i\), and the conditional-rank coordinates above.  The parent-pruned graph returned by \(\mathscr D\) is exactly \(G^\pi\).

Finally, any other DAG \(G'\), mechanism \(\theta'\), and observed world \(W'\) satisfying \cref{obj:ass:positive-normalized-smooth-mechanisms}, \cref{obj:ass:causal-minimality}, \cref{obj:ass:fixed-own-derivative-sign} with the same sign vector \(s\), \cref{obj:ass:shared-diffeomorphic-mixing}, and \cref{obj:ass:one-perfect-intervention-per-node}, and satisfying \(W'.\mathrm{law}=W.\mathrm{law}\), is componentwise \(C^2\)-equivalent to \(W\) up to the simultaneous relabeling encoded by the target permutations.  When \(n=2\), every edge \(j\to i\) of \(G\) has strictly positive observed Gaussian-MMD discrepancy,
\[
0<D_{\pi^{-1}(j),\pi^{-1}(i)}.
\]
Within this regime, \(\mathscr D\) improves the arbitrary-dimensional intervention count of \citet[Theorem~3.4]{vonKugelgenEtAl2023UnknownInterventions} from two perfect interventions per node to one, extends the decoding and uniqueness conclusions from faithful mechanisms to causal-minimal mechanisms, supplies the continuous law-separation witness used by \citet[Theorem~3.2]{vonKugelgenEtAl2023UnknownInterventions} when \(n=2\), and recovers the graph, topological order, and intervention alignment that are inputs in \citet[Theorem~4.2]{WendongEtAl2023CauCA} and \citet[Corollary~{D}.1]{YaoEtAl2025InvariancePrinciple}.

7052dfbafe49e6e49313750befece9738eaebfe5.title: Population MMD discrepancy
7052dfbafe49e6e49313750befece9738eaebfe5.body:
For a complete real Hilbert space \(H\), let \(U\) be a feature map \(r\mapsto \Phi(r)\in H\) with \(\|\Phi(r)\|_H=1\) and
\[
\langle \Phi(a),\Phi(b)\rangle_H=k(a,b)=\exp(-(a-b)^2).
\]
For a mechanism \(\theta\), an observed world \(W\), and \(j,i\in[n]\), define the population MMD discrepancy \(D_{ji}\) by
\[
D_{ji}
=
\left\|
\int \Phi(r)\,d\bigl((R_i)_\# P^0\bigr)(r)
-
\int \Phi(r)\,d\bigl((R_i)_\# P^j\bigr)(r)
\right\|_H .
\]

c21ada7be8d8c5d557cf2e0d75757eed193041c5.title: Empirical MMD discrepancy
c21ada7be8d8c5d557cf2e0d75757eed193041c5.body:
For \(j,i\in[n]\), outcome \(\omega\), and a real Hilbert-space feature map \(U=(\Phi,\ldots)\) of unit norm satisfying \(\langle \Phi(a),\Phi(b)\rangle=k(a,b)=\exp(-(a-b)^2)\), define
\[
\widehat D_{ji}(\omega;U)
=
\left\|
\frac{1}{N_j}\sum_{r=1}^{N_j}\Phi\!\left(\widehat R_i(X^{(j)}_r(\omega))\right)
-
\frac{1}{N_0}\sum_{r=1}^{N_0}\Phi\!\left(\widehat R_i(X^{(0)}_r(\omega))\right)
\right\|_{\mathcal H}.
\]

1cd10de084c11b99d7c01b02c0b1e13a2803278f.title: Second-moment contrast
1cd10de084c11b99d7c01b02c0b1e13a2803278f.body:
For an observed world with environment laws \(P^0,\ldots,P^n\) and likelihood-ratio carriers \(R_i\), define, for \(j,i\in[n]\),
\[
F_{ji}
=
\int_{\mathcal X} R_i(x)^2\,dP^j(x)
-
\int_{\mathcal X} R_i(x)^2\,dP^0(x).
\]

9b8327914311c655d7eaf6682db9a6bee224b424.title: Sample-split experiment world
9b8327914311c655d7eaf6682db9a6bee224b424.body:
A sample-split experiment for a fixed observed environment family \(W\), with latent state space \(\mathbb R^n\), consists of a measurable sample space \(\Omega\) together with:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Experiment law.)} A measure on \(\Omega\).
\item \textbf{(Evaluation fold.)} Environment sample sizes \(N_e\in\mathbb N\), for \(e=0,\ldots,n\), and evaluation latent states
\[
X^{\mathrm{eval}}_{e,m}:\Omega\to\mathbb R^n,
\qquad
m=1,\ldots,N_e .
\]
\item \textbf{(Training fold.)} Training sample sizes \(N^{\mathrm{tr}}_e\in\mathbb N\), for \(e=0,\ldots,n\), and training latent states
\[
X^{\mathrm{tr}}_{e,m}:\Omega\to\mathbb R^n,
\qquad
m=1,\ldots,N^{\mathrm{tr}}_e .
\]
\item \textbf{(Fitted ratios.)} For each full training fold \(T=\{T_{e,m}:e=0,\ldots,n,\ m=1,\ldots,N^{\mathrm{tr}}_e\}\), each \(i\in[n]\), and each \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), a fitted ratio value
\[
\widehat R_i(T,x)\in\mathbb R .
\]
For every \(i\), the map \((T,x)\mapsto \widehat R_i(T,x)\) is jointly measurable; for every \(T\) and \(i\), the map \(x\mapsto \widehat R_i(T,x)\) is measurable; and
\[
\widehat R_i(T,x)>0
\]
for every \(T\), \(i\), and \(x\).
\item \textbf{(First-stage radius.)} A first-stage radius \(a_N(\eta)\in\mathbb R\), indexed by the first-stage failure level \(\eta\), satisfying
\[
a_N(\eta)\ge 0
\]
for every \(\eta\in\mathbb R\).
\item \textbf{(Error levels.)} A familywise evaluation error level \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) and a first-stage failure level \(\eta\in(0,1)\).
\end{itemize}

b14a950998a76d1f707d39b96aca710b94b0a8a3.title: Permuted environment graph
b14a950998a76d1f707d39b96aca710b94b0a8a3.body:
For an observed world \(W\) with target permutation \(\pi\), the environment-label DAG \(G^\pi\) is the directed graph on \([n]\) whose edge relation is
\[
j\to_{G^\pi} i
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
G\text{ has the edge }\pi(j)\to \pi(i),
\qquad j,i\in[n].
\]

18c5f019d72041955238924aed57f512baf296aa.title: Observed conditional CDF
18c5f019d72041955238924aed57f512baf296aa.body:
For an observed probability-law family \(P^0,\ldots,P^n\), an ordering, and a vertex \(i\), let \(B_i\) be the predecessors of \(i\) in that ordering. The symbol
\[
C_i:\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{B_i}\to[0,1]
\]
denotes the following law-selected conditional distribution function. If there exists a map \(C:\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{B_i}\to[0,1]\) such that \(C(t,\ell)\) is jointly measurable in \((t,\ell)\), agrees at each fixed threshold \(t\) almost surely with the raw regular conditional CDF of \(L_i\) given \(L_{B_i}=\ell\) under the observed target-\(i\) law, agrees almost surely with that same raw conditional CDF under the joint law of \((L_i,L_{B_i})\), and is continuous on the observed support of \((L_i,L_{B_i})\), then \(C_i\) is one such map selected from the observed laws alone. Otherwise,
\[
C_i(t\mid L_{B_i}=\ell)=
\begin{cases}
\widetilde C_i(t,\ell), & \widetilde C_i(t,\ell)\in[0,1],\\
0, & \widetilde C_i(t,\ell)\notin[0,1],
\end{cases}
\]
where \(\widetilde C_i(t,\ell)\) is the raw regular conditional CDF of \(L_i\) given \(L_{B_i}=\ell\) under the observed target-\(i\) law.

f0f558128a94b523b13becde6c820c3ddea3c3c7.title: Generated-rank analysis handle
f0f558128a94b523b13becde6c820c3ddea3c3c7.body: \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{rank}}\), the generated-rank proof-strategy handle, records a nonassertive construction for \(\widehat U_i\), the proposed second-stage cross-fitted rank estimator. The estimator \(\widehat U_i\) is formed by adapting Xie's local-linear conditional-CDF estimator to cross-fitted fitted log-ratio responses and cross-fitted conditioning covariates. The handle decomposes the second-stage rank error into the oracle conditional-CDF process, indicator boundary crossings from the generated threshold, and local-design perturbations from generated conditioning arguments; it then linearizes the local-design perturbation component using the generated-covariate expansion of Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle. The second-stage weight convention, bandwidth selector, influence representation, attainment claim, and sharpness claim are treated as open components outside the supplied handle.

31a6c6d83630b42982c58dc0e8e6c998d5875cc9.title: Edge separation set
31a6c6d83630b42982c58dc0e8e6c998d5875cc9.body:
For a target-label permutation \(\pi\), define
\[
\mathcal V_{G,s,\pi}
=
\left\{
\theta\in\Theta_{G,s}:
F^{\mathrm{can}}_{\pi^{-1}(j),\pi^{-1}(i)}(\theta;\pi)\ne0
\text{ for every edge }j\to i\text{ of }G
\right\}.
\]
Here \(F^{\mathrm{can}}_{ab}(\theta;\pi)\) is the second-moment contrast in the canonical observed world generated by \(\theta\) and \(\pi\):
\[
F^{\mathrm{can}}_{ab}(\theta;\pi)
=
\int
\left(
\frac{q_{\pi(b)}(v_{\pi(b)})}
     {p_{\pi(b)}(v_{\pi(b)}\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_G(\pi(b))})}
\right)^2
\,dP^{\pi(a)}(v)
-
\int
\left(
\frac{q_{\pi(b)}(v_{\pi(b)})}
     {p_{\pi(b)}(v_{\pi(b)}\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_G(\pi(b))})}
\right)^2
\,dP^0(v).
\]

745cc65e5f1401766afcb05d9d6a8396ad335c73.title: Cover-separated mechanisms
745cc65e5f1401766afcb05d9d6a8396ad335c73.body:
Let \(H\) be a complete real Hilbert space, and let
\(U=(\Phi,\|\Phi(\cdot)\|,\langle\Phi(\cdot),\Phi(\cdot)\rangle)\) be a feature map satisfying
\[
\|\Phi(r)\|=1,
\qquad
\langle \Phi(a),\Phi(b)\rangle_{\mathbb R}=k(a,b),
\qquad
k(a,b)=\exp\{-(a-b)^2\}.
\]
For a permutation \(\pi\) of \([n]\), define \(\mathcal U_{G,s,\pi}(U)\) to be the set of all \(\theta\in\Theta_{G,s}\) from \(\cref{obj:def:model-stratum}\) such that, for every ancestral cover \(j\lessdot_G i\),
\[
0<
\left\|
\mu_U\!\left(\mathcal L_0^{\,\theta,\pi,\pi^{-1}(i)}\right)
-
\mu_U\!\left(\mathcal L_{\pi^{-1}(j)}^{\,\theta,\pi,\pi^{-1}(i)}\right)
\right\|.
\]
Here the laws are those induced by the canonical observed world generated from \(\theta\) and \(\pi\): the mixing and unmixing maps are identities, the target permutation is \(\pi\), the environment laws are \(P^0=\mathcal L(\theta)\) and \(P^e=\mathcal L(\operatorname{do}(\pi(e))\,\theta)\), and the ratio coordinate in environment \(e\) at latent state \(v\) is
\[
\frac{q_{\pi(e)}(v_{\pi(e)})}{p_{\pi(e)}(v\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_G(\pi(e))})}.
\]

421abec7ffbaeecf1a47b0d21bfd285029f05e3a.title: Sparse witness certificate
421abec7ffbaeecf1a47b0d21bfd285029f05e3a.body:
For every sign vector \(s\in\{-1,1\}^3\), let \(\theta^{\mathrm{sp}}\) be the construction in \cref{obj:def:sparse-witness} and let \(\theta^{\mathrm{can}}\) be the construction in \cref{obj:def:cancellation-witness}, both on the three-node DAG \(1\to2\) with node \(3\) isolated. Let \(W^{\mathrm{sp}}\) and \(W^{\mathrm{can}}\) be the corresponding observed worlds with identity mixing and identity target permutation, so that environment \(0\) has the observational law, environment \(e\) has the intervention law at target \(e\), and
\[
R_i(v)=\frac{q_i(v_i)}{p_i(v_i\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)})}.
\]
Then:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sparse witness regularity.)} The mechanism \(\theta^{\mathrm{sp}}\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:positive-normalized-smooth-mechanisms}, \cref{obj:ass:fixed-own-derivative-sign} with sign vector \(s\), and \cref{obj:ass:faithfulness}. Moreover, every observational conditional density \(p_i^{\mathrm{sp}}\) is \(C^\infty\) on \([0,1]^3\), and every intervention density \(q_i^{\mathrm{sp}}\) is \(C^\infty\) on \([0,1]\).
\item \textbf{(Cancellation witness regularity.)} The mechanism \(\theta^{\mathrm{can}}\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:positive-normalized-smooth-mechanisms}, \cref{obj:ass:fixed-own-derivative-sign} with sign vector \(s\), and \cref{obj:ass:faithfulness}. Moreover, every observational conditional density \(p_i^{\mathrm{can}}\) is \(C^\infty\) on \([0,1]^3\), and every intervention density \(q_i^{\mathrm{can}}\) is \(C^\infty\) on \([0,1]\).
\item \textbf{(Sparse witness separation.)} The sparse witness has
\[
\frac{3}{10000}
<
\int R_2(x)^2\,dP^0_{\mathrm{sp}}(x)
-
\int R_2(x)^2\,dP^1_{\mathrm{sp}}(x),
\]
and its Gaussian-kernel population discrepancy satisfies
\[
\frac{5}{100000000}<D_{12}(W^{\mathrm{sp}}).
\]
\item \textbf{(Cancellation witness equality.)} For the cancellation witness, the law of \(R_2\) under the observational environment equals the law of \(R_2\) under environment \(1\), and
\[
D_{12}(W^{\mathrm{can}})=0.
\]
\end{itemize}

7b707ca0d18e82d34e467f7b96908c929f5151e8.title: Analytic edge perturbation
7b707ca0d18e82d34e467f7b96908c929f5151e8.body:
After the harmless target relabeling \(\pi=\operatorname{id}\), fix the ambient number \(n\) of scalar latent variables, a finite labeled DAG \(G\) on \([n]\), a sign vector \(s\in\{-1,1\}^{[n]}\), a mechanism \(\theta\in\Theta_{G,s}\) as in \cref{obj:def:model-stratum}, and an edge \(j\to i\) of \(G\). Assume that the identity-target canonical observed world generated by \(\theta\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:one-perfect-intervention-per-node}. Let \(\theta^t\) be the edge-specific affine path of \cref{obj:def:affine-path}, and write \(F_{ji}(\eta)\) for the direct-edge second-moment contrast computed in the identity-target canonical observed world generated by a mechanism \(\eta\). Along this path,
\[
F_{ji}(\theta^t)
=
\int_{[0,1]^n}
\frac{(q_i^t(v_i))^2\bigl(q_j^t(v_j)-p_j^t(v_j\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_G(j)})\bigr)
\prod_{\ell\ne i,j}p_\ell^t(v_\ell\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_G(\ell)})}
{p_i^t(v_i\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)})}
\,dv .
\]
There is an open set \(O\subseteq\mathbb R\) with \([0,1]\subseteq O\) such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Integral identity.)} For every \(t\in O\), the displayed integral equals \(F_{ji}(\theta^t)\).
\item \textbf{(Analyticity.)} The map \(t\mapsto F_{ji}(\theta^t)\) is real analytic on a neighborhood of every point of \(O\).
\item \textbf{(Isolated zeros.)} If \(t\in O\) and \(F_{ji}(\theta^t)=0\), then there is \(\varepsilon>0\) such that every \(u\in(t-\varepsilon,t+\varepsilon)\) with \(u\ne t\) satisfies \(F_{ji}(\theta^u)\ne0\).
\end{itemize}
Moreover, \(F_{ji}(\theta^1)\ne0\). Finally, for every relative \(C^2\) neighborhood \(N\) of \(\theta\), there exists \(t\in(0,1)\) such that \(\theta^t\in N\), \(\theta^t\in\Theta_{G,s}\), and \(F_{ji}(\theta^t)\ne0\).

f7f7f0b1795fdca352eb925abd467830ef6c2bb9.title: Observed world data
f7f7f0b1795fdca352eb925abd467830ef6c2bb9.body:
For a mechanism \(\theta\) on the labeled DAG \(G\) with ambient vertex set \([n]\), an observed world is the following data:
\[
\bigl(f,\mathrm{unmix},\pi,(P^e)_{e=0}^n,(R_i)_{i\in[n]}\bigr).
\]
Here \(f\) and \(\mathrm{unmix}\) are maps from the latent state space \(\mathbb R^{[n]}\) to itself, \(\pi\) is a permutation of \([n]\), \(P^e\) is a measure on \(\mathbb R^{[n]}\) for each environment \(e\in\{0,\ldots,n\}\), and \(R_i:\mathbb R^{[n]}\to\mathbb R\) is a real-valued ratio carrier for each target \(i\in[n]\).

41f99ae58adeb00df4bc6f4f7a4474ad2933d999.title: Edge affine path
41f99ae58adeb00df4bc6f4f7a4474ad2933d999.body:
For a finite labeled DAG \(G\) on \([n]\), a sign vector \(s\in\{-1,1\}^{[n]}\), a stratum point \(\theta=((p_\ell,q_\ell))_{\ell=1}^n\in\Theta_{G,s}\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:model-stratum}\), an edge \(j\to i\) in \(G\), and \(t\in[0,1]\), define the reflected edge-specific sparse endpoint \(\theta^{\mathrm{sp}}=((p_\ell^{\mathrm{sp}},q_\ell^{\mathrm{sp}}))_{\ell=1}^n\) in \(G\) by
\[
p_\ell^{\mathrm{sp}}(v)=
\begin{cases}
1+\dfrac{1}{10}\,h(\operatorname{reflect}(s_j,v_j))\,h(\operatorname{reflect}(s_i,v_i)), & \ell=i,\\
1, & \ell\ne i,
\end{cases}
\qquad
q_\ell^{\mathrm{sp}}(z)=
\dfrac{4\exp(4\,\operatorname{reflect}(s_\ell,z))}{\exp(4)-1},
\]
where \(h(x)=2x-1\). The affine path \(\theta^t=((p_\ell^t,q_\ell^t))_{\ell=1}^n\) is the mechanism on \(G\) with
\[
p_\ell^t(v)=(1-t)p_\ell(v)+t\,p_\ell^{\mathrm{sp}}(v),
\qquad
q_\ell^t(z)=(1-t)q_\ell(z)+t\,q_\ell^{\mathrm{sp}}(z),
\qquad \ell\in[n].
\]

100a3d1355154e8f921ada86bf43920d6d1e7157.title: Componentwise \(C^2\) equivalence
100a3d1355154e8f921ada86bf43920d6d1e7157.body:
For \(m=1,2\), let \(W_m\) be an observed world over \((G_m,\theta_m)\) with mixing map \(f_m\), inverse-coordinate map \(g_m\), target permutation \(\pi_m\), and observed laws \((P_m^e)_{e=0}^n\). With the same ambient number \(n\) of scalar latent variables, write
\[
\mathcal X_m=\{f_m(v):v\in[0,1]^n\},\qquad m=1,2.
\]
The worlds \(W_1\) and \(W_2\) are componentwise \(C^2\)-equivalent when the following conditions hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Observed support.)} Their observed supports agree:
\[
\mathcal X_1=\mathcal X_2.
\]
\item \textbf{(DAG relabeling.)} There is a permutation \(\sigma\) of \([n]\) such that, for every \(j,i\in[n]\),
\[
\sigma(j)\to_{G_2}\sigma(i)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
j\to_{G_1} i.
\]
\item \textbf{(Target alignment.)} For every \(e\in[n]\),
\[
\pi_2(e)=\sigma(\pi_1(e)).
\]
\item \textbf{(Coordinate changes.)} There are real functions \(h_i\) and \(\bar h_i\), one pair for each \(i\in[n]\), whose restrictions to \([0,1]\) are \(C^2\) and map \([0,1]\) into \([0,1]\), such that, for every \(i\in[n]\) and every \(z\in[0,1]\),
\[
\bar h_i(h_i(z))=z,
\qquad
h_i(\bar h_i(z))=z.
\]
\item \textbf{(Unmixing relation.)} For every \(x\in\mathcal X_1\) and every \(i\in[n]\),
\[
g_2(x)_{\sigma(i)}
=
h_i\!\left(g_1(x)_i\right).
\]
\end{itemize}

21d870ee5990a1220b3382f37a8e297c91ecdded.title: Exact ratio decoding
21d870ee5990a1220b3382f37a8e297c91ecdded.body:
Fix \(n\), a finite labelled DAG \(G\) on \([n]\), and a sign vector \(s\in\{-1,+1\}^{[n]}\). Let \(\theta=(p_i,q_i)_{i\in[n]}\) be a mechanism on \(G\). Let \(W\) be its observed world, with shared mixing map \(f\), inverse map \(f^{-1}\), target permutation \(\pi\), observed laws \((P^0,\ldots,P^n)\), likelihood ratios \(R_i=dP^i/dP^0\), and log-ratios \(L_i=\log R_i\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Smooth positive mechanisms.)} \(\theta\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:positive-normalized-smooth-mechanisms}.
\item \textbf{(Causal minimality.)} \(\theta\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:causal-minimality}.
\item \textbf{(Shared mixing.)} The maps \(f\) and \(f^{-1}\) in \(W\) satisfy \cref{obj:ass:shared-diffeomorphic-mixing}.
\item \textbf{(One intervention per node.)} The laws \((P^0,\ldots,P^n)\), ratios \((R_i)_{i\in[n]}\), and target permutation \(\pi\) in \(W\) satisfy \cref{obj:ass:one-perfect-intervention-per-node}.
\item \textbf{(Own-derivative signs.)} \(\theta\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:fixed-own-derivative-sign} with sign vector \(s\).
\item \textbf{(Cover separation.)} The stratum point \(\theta\in\Theta_{G,s}\) belongs to the cover-separated set \(\mathcal U_{G,s,\pi}(U)\) of \cref{obj:def:cover-separated-set} for the Gaussian feature map \(U\), i.e. the unit-norm feature map whose kernel is \(k(a,b)=\exp\{-(a-b)^2\}\).
\end{itemize}
Let \(\mathscr D\) be the population decoder of \cref{obj:def:population-decoder}, let \(H_D=\{j\to i:D_{ji}>0\}\), and let \(G^\pi\) be the environment-label DAG. Then
\[
\operatorname{TC}(H_D)=\operatorname{TC}(G^\pi).
\]
The ordering selected by \(\mathscr D\) is a topological ordering of \(H_D\). For every topological ordering of \(H_D\), with predecessor set \(B_i\) for node \(i\), and every \(i\in[n]\), the selected conditional CDF \(C_i(t\mid L_{B_i})\) is a continuous version of the conditional ratio CDF. For each such \(i\), there exists a continuous version \(C\) such that, for every \(t\) and every latent state \(v\) in the latent cube,
\[
C\bigl(t,L_{B_i}(f(v))\bigr)
=
\Pr_{\theta}\{L_i\le t\mid L_{B_i}=L_{B_i}(f(v))\}
\]
with target coordinate \(\pi(i)\) as specified by the structural conditional-ratio formula. Every continuous version agrees with the selected \(C_i\) on the observed conditional-ratio support, and the selected version satisfies the same displayed identity at every mixed latent point \(f(v)\). Consequently, for every \(v\) in the latent cube,
\[
U_i(f(v))=
\begin{cases}
Q_{\pi(i)}(v_{\pi(i)}), & s_{\pi(i)}=1,\\
1-Q_{\pi(i)}(v_{\pi(i)}), & s_{\pi(i)}=-1.
\end{cases}
\]
For every topological ordering of \(H_D\) and every \(i\in[n]\),
\[
\pi^{-1}\!\bigl(\operatorname{pa}_G(\pi(i))\bigr)\subseteq B_i.
\]
Under \(P^0\), for every such ordering, every \(i\in[n]\), and every \(A\subseteq B_i\),
\[
U_i\perp\!\!\!\perp U_{B_i\setminus A}\mid U_A
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\pi^{-1}\!\bigl(\operatorname{pa}_G(\pi(i))\bigr)\subseteq A.
\]
Thus, for every such ordering and every \(i\), the set
\[
\pi^{-1}\!\bigl(\operatorname{pa}_G(\pi(i))\bigr)
\]
is admissible and is the unique inclusion-minimal admissible parent set. The observed laws are coherent with the displayed observed world: the same family \((P^0,\ldots,P^n)\) supplies the decoder inputs, likelihood ratios \((R_i)_{i\in[n]}\), and conditional-rank coordinates above. The parent-pruned graph returned by \(\mathscr D\) is exactly \(G^\pi\).

Finally, for any other DAG \(G'\), mechanism \(\theta'\), and observed world \(W'\) satisfying \cref{obj:ass:positive-normalized-smooth-mechanisms}, \cref{obj:ass:causal-minimality}, \cref{obj:ass:fixed-own-derivative-sign} with the same sign vector \(s\), \cref{obj:ass:shared-diffeomorphic-mixing}, and \cref{obj:ass:one-perfect-intervention-per-node}, if the observed law family of \(W'\) equals \((P^0,\ldots,P^n)\), then \(W'\) is componentwise \(C^2\)-equivalent to \(W\) up to the simultaneous relabeling encoded by the target permutations. When \(n=2\), every edge \(j\to i\) of \(G\) has strictly positive observed Gaussian-MMD discrepancy,
\[
0<D_{\pi^{-1}(j),\pi^{-1}(i)}.
\]
Within this regime, \(\mathscr D\) improves the arbitrary-dimensional intervention count of \citet[Theorem~3.4]{vonKugelgenEtAl2023UnknownInterventions} from two perfect interventions per node to one, extends the decoding and uniqueness conclusions from faithful mechanisms to causal-minimal mechanisms, supplies the continuous law-separation witness used by \citet[Theorem~3.2]{vonKugelgenEtAl2023UnknownInterventions} when \(n=2\), and recovers the graph, topological order, and intervention alignment that are inputs in \citet[Theorem~4.2]{WendongEtAl2023CauCA} and \citet[Corollary~{D}.1]{YaoEtAl2025InvariancePrinciple}.

68af05bd448e45a9c390fc53de1fffbfdccb2c0b.title: Generic cover separation
68af05bd448e45a9c390fc53de1fffbfdccb2c0b.body:
Let \(n\) be the ambient number of scalar latent variables, let \(G\) be a finite labeled DAG on \([n]\), let \(s\) be a sign vector with coordinates in \(\{-1,1\}\), and let \(\pi\) be a permutation of \([n]\). Suppose that the stratum \(\Theta_{G,s}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:model-stratum}\) is nonempty. Then the direct-edge separation set \(\mathcal V_{G,s,\pi}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:edge-separated-set}\) is open and dense in \(\Theta_{G,s}\), and
\[
\mathcal V_{G,s,\pi}\subseteq \mathcal U_{G,s,\pi}.
\]
Here \(\mathcal U_{G,s,\pi}\) is the ancestral-cover separation set of \(\cref{obj:def:cover-separated-set}\) formed with the Gaussian feature map whose kernel is \(k(a,b)=\exp\{-(a-b)^2\}\). The set \(\mathcal U_{G,s,\pi}\) is open and dense in \(\Theta_{G,s}\), and its complement in \(\Theta_{G,s}\) is meagre, closed, and nowhere dense. If \(G\) has no directed edges, then
\[
\mathcal V_{G,s,\pi}=\Theta_{G,s}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\mathcal U_{G,s,\pi}=\Theta_{G,s}.
\]

2b0d1ac3d764d4877c82a6c207701d953bf0c361.title: Cover-separated mechanisms
2b0d1ac3d764d4877c82a6c207701d953bf0c361.body:
Let \(H\) be a complete real Hilbert space, and let \(U\) be a feature map \(\phi:\mathbb R\to H\) satisfying
\[
\|\phi(r)\|=1
\quad\text{and}\quad
\langle \phi(a),\phi(b)\rangle_H=k(a,b)
\]
for all \(r,a,b\in\mathbb R\).  For a target permutation \(\pi\), let \(W_{\theta,\pi}^{\mathrm{can}}\) denote the canonical observed world generated from \(\theta\) and \(\pi\): it uses the identity mixing and unmixing maps, target permutation \(\pi\), laws \(P^0\) from \(\theta\)'s observational law and \(P^{e+1}\) from the intervention law targeting \(\pi(e)\), and ratio
\[
R_e(v)=\frac{q_{\pi(e)}(v_{\pi(e)})}{p_{\pi(e)}(v)}.
\]
The cover-separated set is
\[
\mathcal U_{G,s,\pi}
=
\left\{
\theta\in\Theta_{G,s}:
0<
\left\|
\int \phi(r)\,d\mathsf P^{0}_{\theta,\pi,\pi^{-1}(i)}(r)
-
\int \phi(r)\,d\mathsf P^{\pi^{-1}(j)}_{\theta,\pi,\pi^{-1}(i)}(r)
\right\|_H
\ \text{for every } j\lessdot_G i
\right\},
\]
where \(\mathsf P^{0}_{\theta,\pi,a}\) is the law of ratio \(a\) under the observational environment of \(W_{\theta,\pi}^{\mathrm{can}}\), and \(\mathsf P^{b}_{\theta,\pi,a}\) is the law of ratio \(a\) under intervention environment \(b\) of \(W_{\theta,\pi}^{\mathrm{can}}\).

ceb83459c2dda75c8a316edc375706d402a55963.title: Exact ratio decoding
ceb83459c2dda75c8a316edc375706d402a55963.body:
Fix \(n\), a finite labelled DAG \(G\) on \([n]\), and a sign vector \(s\in\{-1,+1\}^{[n]}\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Smooth positive mechanisms.)} \(\theta\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:positive-normalized-smooth-mechanisms}.
\item \textbf{(Causal minimality.)} \(\theta\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:causal-minimality}.
\item \textbf{(Shared mixing.)} The maps \(f\) and \(f^{-1}\) in \(W\) satisfy \cref{obj:ass:shared-diffeomorphic-mixing}.
\item \textbf{(One intervention per node.)} The laws \((P^0,\ldots,P^n)\), ratios \((R_i)_{i\in[n]}\), and target permutation \(\pi\) in \(W\) satisfy \cref{obj:ass:one-perfect-intervention-per-node}.
\item \textbf{(Own-derivative signs.)} \(\theta\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:fixed-own-derivative-sign} with sign vector \(s\).
\item \textbf{(Cover separation.)} The stratum point \(\theta\in\Theta_{G,s}\) belongs to the cover-separated set \(\mathcal U_{G,s,\pi}\) of \cref{obj:def:cover-separated-set}, formed with the Gaussian feature map for \(k(a,b)=\exp\{-(a-b)^2\}\).
\end{itemize}
Let \(\mathscr D\) be the population decoder of \cref{obj:def:population-decoder}, let \(H_D=\{j\to i:D_{ji}>0\}\), and let \(G^\pi\) be the environment-label DAG. Then
\[
\operatorname{TC}(H_D)=\operatorname{TC}(G^\pi).
\]
The ordering selected by \(\mathscr D\) is a topological ordering of \(H_D\). For every topological ordering of \(H_D\), with predecessor set \(B_i\) for node \(i\), and every \(i\in[n]\), the selected conditional CDF \(C_i(t\mid L_{B_i})\) is a continuous version of the conditional ratio CDF. For each such \(i\), there exists a continuous version \(C\) agreeing at every latent point \(v\) in the latent cube with the structural conditional-ratio CDF for target coordinate \(\pi(i)\); every continuous version agrees with the selected \(C_i\) on the observed conditional-ratio support, and the selected version satisfies the same structural identity at every mixed latent point \(f(v)\). Consequently, for every \(v\) in the latent cube,
\[
U_i(f(v))=
\begin{cases}
Q_{\pi(i)}(v_{\pi(i)}), & s_{\pi(i)}=1,\\
1-Q_{\pi(i)}(v_{\pi(i)}), & s_{\pi(i)}=-1.
\end{cases}
\]
For every topological ordering of \(H_D\) and every \(i\in[n]\),
\[
\pi^{-1}\!\bigl(\operatorname{pa}_G(\pi(i))\bigr)\subseteq B_i.
\]
Under \(P^0\), for every such ordering, every \(i\in[n]\), and every \(A\subseteq B_i\),
\[
U_i\perp\!\!\!\perp U_{B_i\setminus A}\mid U_A
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\pi^{-1}\!\bigl(\operatorname{pa}_G(\pi(i))\bigr)\subseteq A.
\]
Thus, for every such ordering and every \(i\), the set
\[
\pi^{-1}\!\bigl(\operatorname{pa}_G(\pi(i))\bigr)
\]
is admissible and is the unique inclusion-minimal admissible parent set. The observed laws are coherent with \(W\), and the parent-pruned graph returned by \(\mathscr D\) is exactly \(G^\pi\).

5bae896722df5cd0d566d8f69292261ae600706e.title: Generic cover separation
5bae896722df5cd0d566d8f69292261ae600706e.body:
Let \(n\) be the ambient number of scalar latent variables. Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Finite labeled DAG.)} \(G\) is a finite labeled DAG on \([n]\).
\item \textbf{(Sign stratum.)} \(s\) is a sign vector with coordinates in \(\{-1,1\}\), and the stratum \(\Theta_{G,s}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:model-stratum}\) is nonempty.
\item \textbf{(Target permutation.)} \(\pi\) is a permutation of \([n]\).
\end{itemize}
Let \(\mathcal V_{G,s,\pi}\) be the direct-edge separation set of \(\cref{obj:def:edge-separated-set}\), and let \(\mathcal U_{G,s,\pi}\) be the ancestral-cover separation set of \(\cref{obj:def:cover-separated-set}\) formed with the Gaussian feature map \(\phi(a)=k(a,\cdot)\) for \(k(a,b)=\exp\{-(a-b)^2\}\). Then \(\mathcal V_{G,s,\pi}\) is open and dense in \(\Theta_{G,s}\), and
\[
\mathcal V_{G,s,\pi}\subseteq \mathcal U_{G,s,\pi}.
\]
Moreover, \(\mathcal U_{G,s,\pi}\) is open and dense in \(\Theta_{G,s}\), and its complement in \(\Theta_{G,s}\) is meagre, closed, and nowhere dense. If \(G\) has no directed edges, then
\[
\mathcal V_{G,s,\pi}=\Theta_{G,s}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\mathcal U_{G,s,\pi}=\Theta_{G,s}.
\]

e549097b337e7124d2cf73cea50720abe69128e2.title: Cover-separated mechanisms
e549097b337e7124d2cf73cea50720abe69128e2.body:
Let \(H\) be a complete real Hilbert space, and let \(U\) be a feature map \(\phi:\mathbb R\to H\) satisfying
\[
\|\phi(r)\|_H=1,
\qquad
\langle \phi(a),\phi(b)\rangle_H=k(a,b)
\]
for all \(r,a,b\in\mathbb R\).  For a target permutation \(\pi\), let \(W_{\theta,\pi}^{\mathrm{can}}\) be the canonical observed world generated by \(\theta\) and \(\pi\): the mixing and unmixing maps are the identity, the target permutation is \(\pi\), the observational environment has law induced by \(\theta\)'s observational law, intervention environment \(e\) has law induced by the intervention targeting \(\pi(e)\), and its ratio carrier is
\[
R_e(v)=
\frac{q_{\pi(e)}(v_{\pi(e)})}
{p_{\pi(e)}(v_{\pi(e)}\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_G(\pi(e))})}.
\]
The cover-separated set is
\[
\mathcal U_{G,s,\pi}
=
\left\{
\theta\in\Theta_{G,s}:
D_{ji}\!\left(W_{\theta,\pi}^{\mathrm{can}}\right)>0
\ \text{for every } j,i\in[n]\text{ with }\pi(j)\lessdot_G\pi(i)
\right\},
\]
where
\[
D_{ji}\!\left(W_{\theta,\pi}^{\mathrm{can}}\right)
=
\left\|
\int \phi(r)\,d\mathsf P^0_{\theta,\pi,i}(r)
-
\int \phi(r)\,d\mathsf P^j_{\theta,\pi,i}(r)
\right\|_H,
\]
\(\mathsf P^0_{\theta,\pi,i}\) is the law of ratio \(i\) under the observational environment of \(W_{\theta,\pi}^{\mathrm{can}}\), and \(\mathsf P^j_{\theta,\pi,i}\) is the law of ratio \(i\) under intervention environment \(j\) of \(W_{\theta,\pi}^{\mathrm{can}}\).

0ffa9495200473692d20f3ba12ada339e960de26.title: Independent environment sampling
0ffa9495200473692d20f3ba12ada339e960de26.body:
The sample-split experiment is carried by a probability law, and each environment law \(P^e\) is a probability measure. It satisfies:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Training fold.)} For each environment \(e\), the training observations are measurable, independent within that environment, and each training observation in environment \(e\) has law \(P^e\).
\item \textbf{(Evaluation fold.)} For each environment \(e\), the evaluation observations are measurable, independent within that environment, and each evaluation observation in environment \(e\) has law \(P^e\).
\item \textbf{(Fold independence.)} The complete training fold is independent of the complete array of evaluation observations across all environments.
\item \textbf{(First-stage measurability.)} For each latent coordinate \(i\in[n]\) and latent state \(x\), the ratio estimate \(\widehat R_i(x)\) is measurable with respect to the training fold, and the same estimate is jointly measurable in the training fold and \(x\). The training-fold event
\[
\left\{\omega:\ \forall i\in[n],\ \forall e,\ 
\int \left|\widehat R_i(x)-R_i(x)\right|\,dP^e(x)\le a_N(\eta)
\ \text{with finite integral}\right\}
\]
is measurable with respect to the training fold.
\end{itemize}
